The finished trolley must undergo visual and mechanical alignment checks. The structural frame work must be completely free from warp, twist, or joint distortion.

Classifies compressors into three service envelopes based on evaporating temperature: LBP (-35°C to -10°C), MBP (-20°C to +10°C), and HBP (comfort AC at -5°C to +13.9°C, commercial heat pumps at -23.3°C to +12.8°C).
If a compressor is rated for a voltage range (e.g., 220–240 V), type and performance testing must be executed at the calculated mathematical mean voltage (e.g., 230 V).

To verify motor starting torque under equalized pressure conditions, the compressor is subjected to a Saturated Start Test with saturated evaporating/condensing temperatures set based on back-pressure grade: LBP at 15.0°C, MBP at 32.2°C, and HBP at 32.2°C.

The start test must be conducted for a duration of 3 hours or until the steel shell temperature stabilizes within ±5°C, using the higher rated voltage in dual-rated systems, while maintaining a minimum COP of 90.0% of its rated baseline.
The electrical insulation resistance measured between the motor windings and the compressor's steel housing must not be less than 2 MΩ.
The fully assembled steel housing must be tested pneumatically using dry air, nitrogen, or helium at a test pressure of 1.0 MPa (gauge) and must show zero leakage.
Calibrates housing test pressure to non-subcritical refrigerants: R-134a (CF3CH2F) at 6.5 MPa (65 Bar), R-22 (CHClF2) at 10.5 MPa (105 Bar), and R-600a (CH(CH3)3) at 3.5 MPa (35 Bar).
If a specialized compressor's design operating envelope lies outside standard parameters, testing must be carried out at the worst-case condition within the manufacturer's defined operating envelope.

Under the November 2020 amendment, starting tests are restricted to single-phase induction motor compressors only, and units must start and run at the minimum of the voltage range defined by the compressor specification.

certification.description: Mandatory Testing Compliance. Under Municipal Corporation bylaws, state public works department (PWD) guidelines, and solid waste management rules across Indian cities, suppliers of waste management gear must provide test certificates from a NABL-accredited laboratory verifying that their mobile containers successfully withstand the 18-test sequence of IS 12402 (Part 2) before bidding on public tenders.
requirements: Any numerical value representing the final observed or calculated result of a physical dimension, water temperature, deflection percentage, or drop height must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

Before executing any physical tests, a detailed visual inspection of the container must be performed to check that it is completely undamaged, has no manufacturing defects, and to establish a comparison log to measure structural changes.
It must be verified that all structural sizing, nominal volumes, gripping/lifting interfaces, and wheel configurations conform to the specifications of IS 12402 (Part 1).

Containers made of plastic material (entirely or in part) must be conditioned in a temperature chamber prior to physical testing: (a) at -18 ± 3°C for a minimum of 12 hours, and (b) at +60 ± 5°C for a minimum of 12 hours.
Waste containers manufactured entirely of metal are explicitly exempted from undergoing extreme hot or cold thermal chamber conditioning.
For testing normal 'N' type containers, the test ballast density must equal 0.4 kg/dm³ (representing average refuse density of 0.2 kg/dm³ multiplied by a safety factor of 2).
For testing reinforced 'R' type containers, the test ballast density must equal 1.0 kg/dm³ (representing average refuse density of 0.5 kg/dm³ multiplied by a safety factor of 2).
The test ballast must consist of a uniform mix of metal parts (such as long bolts) and rubber balls. The ballast must occupy exactly 90 percent of the total capacity of the container.

Test loads (including container and ballast weight) are strictly calibrated based on volume and type (e.g., 120-litre Type N = 0.48 kN, Type R = 1.20 kN; 240-litre Type N = 0.96 kN, Type R = 2.40 kN; 1000-litre Type N = 4.00 kN, Type R = 10.00 kN).

The standard specifies a strict, progressive sequence of 18 tests (starting with Test 1 check on deflection, Test 2 brim capacity, Test 7 free fall drop, Test 8 inclined impact, up to Test 18 final deflection check) to evaluate progressive structural fatigue.
Under Test 1 and Test 18, the empty container is measured at the gripping plane, and the maximum permissible deflection must not exceed 10/1000 (1.0% of nominal overall width).
Under Test 2, capacity is verified by placing the container level in a receipt tank and filling simultaneously with water at 15 ± 5°C to measure the exact volume of water held at the brim.
Under Test 7, the loaded container is subjected to a vertical drop test consisting of exactly 50 falls (25 falls with the lid closed, 25 falls with the lid open).
Under Test 7, Class A containers (120, 240, 330 litres) must be dropped from a vertical height of 160 mm to simulate rolling off steps and curbs.
Under Test 7, Class B containers (500, 750, 1000 litres) must be dropped from a vertical height of 140 mm (which corresponds to the average height of a standard pavement edge).
After the 50-drop test, the container must show zero permanent deformation, zero weld cracks, and zero damage making it unfit for use. Castors and pivots must remain completely free to rotate.

Under Test 8, the loaded container is mounted on a test truck on a 10° incline and released to strike a rigid wall. It must withstand a total of 80 impacts (across faces 1-4 and edges 1-2, 2-3, 3-4, 4-1) with a truck travel of 1.0 m (faces) or 0.5 m (edges).

The hose reinforcement must consist of multiple plies (typically 2 to 6 layers) of high-strength spiral steel wire or steel wire braids, interspersed with heavy-duty synthetic textile fabric plies to ensure maximum burst resistance.
The outer cover must be formed of wrapped weather, ozone, and abrasion-resistant synthetic rubber to protect the steel wire core from UV rays, derrick friction, and structural impacts on-site.

Every finished hose assembly must undergo a factory hydrostatic proof test at 1.5 to 2.0 times the rated working pressure (WP) for a minimum of 10 minutes, demonstrating zero leaks, seepage, or permanent swelling.

To prevent catastrophic on-site failures, the minimum burst pressure (destructive test) of any representative prototype hose assembly must be at least 2.5 times its rated working pressure (e.g., minimum burst of 12,500 psi for a 5,000 psi working hose).
To prevent structural kinking and line constriction, hoses must satisfy minimum bending curves without buckling (e.g., a 100 mm / 4-in hose typically requires a minimum bend radius of 1600 mm).

Hoses must be equipped with factory swaged or built-in end connections containing API line pipe threads, forged hammer unions (e.g., Fig 1002/1502), or flanges, tested simultaneously to ensure zero joint slip.

certification.description: Mandatory Certification and Procedural Compliance under the Gas Cylinder Rules of the Government of India, in coordination with the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO). All active LPG bottling plants must maintain strict audit logs verifying that 100% of filled cylinders pass the visual inspection, gross-weight verification, and soapy water leak checks mandated by IS 15966.
requirements: Before filling, operators must visually check that the cylinder belongs to the authorized marketing company or distributor network to prevent illegal cross-filling.

Inspectors must verify that the cylinder's periodic hydrostatic test date (marked on the stay plate/collar) has not expired. Cylinders due or overdue for testing must be segregated immediately for periodic testing under IS 16054.
Mandates inspecting the cylinder shell for physical integrity prior to filling using strict rejection thresholds (bulges, cuts, dents, cracks, lamination, and digs).

A bulge is defined as a visible swelling of the cylinder wall, which alters the original calculated cylindrical geometry, representing a severe localized yielding under pressure. Rejection is mandatory in all cases.

A dent represents a localized depression. If the width of the dent is greater than 2 percent of the external cylinder diameter, the unit must be rejected if: a) its depth is greater than 1/10th of the mean dent diameter, b) its depth exceeds 25 percent of its width, or c) the dent lies on or adjacent to a weld joint.

A cut represents a sharp impression where metal has been removed or redistributed. It must be rejected if it is 75 mm or more in length, or if the undamaged remaining wall thickness is less than the minimum calculated wall thickness.
Intersecting cuts (the point of intersection of two or more cuts) represent a high-stress concentration zone susceptible to rapid crack propagation. Rejection is mandatory in all cases.

Cracks (splits or rifts in the shell) and laminations (layering of materials appearing as discontinuities) compromise the pressure-bearing capacity of low-carbon steel. Rejection is mandatory in all cases.
A dig represents a sharp depression where the surface metal has been physically penetrated. It must be rejected if its length is 75 mm or more and its width is 4 mm or more.
The actual weight of the clean, empty cylinder must be compared with the stamped tare weight. Abnormal tare weight variances indicate internal scaling or structural steel loss, requiring segregation.

Every cylinder must be checked for positive residual gas pressure. A completely depressurized cylinder indicates a potential open valve that may have allowed moisture, water, or air to enter, requiring internal washing and inspection.

Filled cylinders must be weighed to verify that the net LPG weight matches the rated filling capacity within narrow legal tolerances. Overfilled units represent an extreme thermal expansion hazard and must be safely degassed.

The valve, valve spindle, and bung-joint interface must be tested for leak tightness (using a soap-water solution or a dedicated testing bath). The presence of any bubbles indicating a leak requires immediate evacuation of the LPG.

Observed or calculated weights, test pressures, and dimension limits must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

Valve pad threads must be thoroughly cleaned of paint and residue using a soft wire brush and checked in accordance with IS 9121 using a standard 3/4" 14 NGT thread plug gauge.

Every cylinder that passes the visual inspections must be subjected to a hydrostatic proof pressure test at a test pressure of 2.45 MPa (25.00 kgf/cm²). The test pressure must be held with zero drop or leakage.

Following successful completion of the hydrostatic test, all residual testing water must be drained, and air must be removed by press-opening the valve using a suitable adaptor. Storing any cylinder with internal air pressure is strictly prohibited.

Establishes a strict visual rejection framework for physical defects on the cylinder wall under Table 1, including bulges, dents, cuts, digs, cracks, laminations, and foot ring bottom clearance limits.
A bulge (visible swelling) or a crack (split or rift in the shell) compromises structural safety. Rejection is mandatory in all cases.

A dent (localized depression) requires rejection if its depth exceeds 1/10th of its mean diameter, its mean diameter exceeds 1/4th of the cylinder diameter, or if it lies on or adjacent to a weld joint.
A cut or gouge requires rejection if its length is 75 mm or more, or if the remaining wall thickness in the affected portion is less than the minimum calculated wall thickness.
A dig (surface penetration) requires rejection if its length is 75 mm or more and its width is 4 mm or more.

Footring bottom clearance (distance of body bottom from the ground) must not be less than 8 mm for cylinders up to 34 litres water capacity, 15 mm for cylinders between 34 to 50 litres, and 25 mm for cylinders exceeding 50 litres.

Establishes maximum depth limits for corrosion. Isolated pits, area corrosion (not exceeding 20% surface), line corrosion, and crevice corrosion require rejection if the depth of penetration exceeds 0.4 mm.

Cylinders passing inspection must be stamped on the valve collar stay plate in the format '09 A - XX', where '09' represents the year of testing, 'A' indicates the month (A=Jan, B=Feb, etc.), and 'XX' represents the monthly control number.
All inspection, visual, hydrostatic, and pneumatic testing logs must be digitally recorded and maintained in a computerized database for the entire operational life of the cylinder.

Observed or calculated dimensions, defect depths, weights, and test pressures must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Drums and Tins (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT), Government of India, all Large Fixed-End Steel Drums (Grade A and Grade B) must conform to IS 1783 (Part 1 and Part 2) and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified drums in India is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Exemption is granted solely for export-oriented shipments and pre-filled imported containers. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial steel packaging.
requirements: Every certified fixed-end steel drum must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 1783 Part 1 or Part 2) stenciled on the drum body or ends.
The nominal capacity must be 200 Litres, and the minimum gross capacity must be at least 210 Litres when measured with water at ambient temperature.

Grade A drums are heavy-duty containers constructed from cold-reduced steel sheets of nominal thickness 1.25 mm for both the cylindrical body and end plates. Ends must be double-seamed (Type 1) or spiral/triple-seamed (Type 2) to ensure maximum mechanical strength.

Grade B drums are standard-duty containers. Type 1 utilized 1.25 mm nominal sheet thickness for both the body and ends with double-seamed end seams. Type 2 utilizes slightly thinner steel sheets of 1.00 mm nominal thickness with spiral or triple-seamed ends.
The longitudinal body seam must be continuously resistance welded to provide a completely air-tight and robust joint.

Every single drum must be tested for leak-tightness before dispatch. The drum must withstand an internal air pressure of 0.3 kg/cm² to 0.5 kg/cm² (depending on grade/type) while submerged in water or sprayed with a soap solution, showing zero bubbles, leaks, or structural sweating.

To guarantee structural safety during rough handling or transportation accidents, the drum is filled with water to 98 percent of its gross capacity and dropped from a specified height (e.g. 1.2 meters) onto a solid concrete or steel pad. It must show zero splits, structural tears, or leakage.

The drum must withstand a high internal hydrostatic pressure (e.g., 1.5 to 2.0 kg/cm² or 150-200 kPa for Grade A) for a minimum of 5 minutes without showing any signs of leakage, sweating, seam slippage, or permanent warping.

The interior of each drum must be completely clean, dry, and free from scale, rust, or foreign matter. If the raw steel sheet is incompatible with the product to be filled, a suitable protective lining, lacquer, or epoxy coating must be applied.

A lot comprises up to 300 drums (or 1,000 kg, whichever is greater) of the same grade, size, and condition. Random samples are selected for visual, dimensional, and destructive physical testing. Non-conforming defectives must stay within strictly bounded acceptance limits, or the entire lot is rejected.

certification.description: Mandatory Certification under the Gas Cylinder Rules of the Government of India, in direct coordination with the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO). All LPG cylinders manufactured, imported, or sold in India must carry the prestigious physical ISI 'Standard Mark' stamped on the stay plate, alongside a unique manufacturer license number (CM/L), to legally enter commercial or domestic distribution.
requirements: Final observed or calculated test and analytical values (such as wall thickness, burst pressure, and expansion) must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

Calculates nominal wall thickness (t) using the formula t = (P * D_o) / (2 * f * J + P), where J is the joint efficiency factor, P is test pressure (normally 2.44 MPa), and f is the allowable design stress (based on the minimum yield strength of the low-carbon steel).
The absolute minimum wall thickness for cylinders of nominal water capacity exceeding 5 litres must not be less than 1.5 mm, regardless of calculation results.

Every finished cylinder must withstand a hydrostatic proof pressure test at a test pressure of 2.44 MPa / 25 bar (or as designed up to 2.50 MPa) for a minimum of 30 seconds showing zero leakage, sweating, or permanent deformation.
Finished cylinders must undergo pneumatic leak testing at a pressure of at least 1.2 MPa (12 bar) using dry compressed air while submerged in a water bath, showing zero bubbles.
One cylinder from every manufactured lot of 403 or less must be burst hydraulically, requiring a minimum burst pressure of 4.90 MPa / 50 bar and nominal hoop stress at burst of at least 332.5 MPa.

Under Amendment No. 5 (June 2026), the volumetric expansion ratio at burst must be >=20% (or >=14% if length is <= diameter) when the steel's tensile strength is <410 N/mm²; and >=15% (or >=10% if length is <= diameter) when tensile strength is >=410 N/mm².

Cylinders must withstand 80,000 cycles without failure at an upper cyclic pressure equal to two-thirds of the hydrostatic test pressure (UCP = 2/3 * Ph), with the lower cyclic pressure <= 10% of the upper pressure and frequency <= 0.25 Hz (15 cycles/min).

Alternatively, cylinders must withstand 12,000 cycles without failure at an upper cyclic pressure equal to the full hydrostatic test pressure (UCP = Ph) under identical lower-pressure and frequency limits.

Under Amendment No. 5 (June 2026), the foot ring must be welded at least 20 mm away from the circumferential weld of the cylinder body. Sheet thickness of the foot ring must be >= the calculated wall thickness of the cylinder shell.

Under Amendment No. 5 (June 2026), minimum ground clearance of the bottom shell must be >= 8 mm for cylinders up to 34 litres water capacity, >= 15 mm for cylinders between 34 to 50 litres capacity, and >= 25 mm for cylinders exceeding 50 litres capacity.
Under Amendment No. 5 (June 2026), cylinders must carry a permanent, tamper-proof barcode, QR code, or RFID tag as approved by statutory authorities, to enable machine-readable digital tracking.

However, state government ropeway safety acts, municipal municipal-corporation clearances, and forest/environmental department permits across India make strict compliance with IS 5230 mandatory for ropeway licensing, safety certification, and commercial operation.
requirements: Final observed or calculated test and analytical values (such as clearances, specific speeds, friction limits, or dimensions) must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960 (or IS 2:2022). The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
The crossing of routes, roads, railways, waterways, or other ropeways shall be avoided as far as possible to prevent mechanical collisions or clearance hazards.
Where crossings are unavoidable, vertical and horizontal clearances must be determined in such a manner that there is no danger for any vehicle using the various ways.

Crossings and paralleling with railways, highways, cableways, or overhead electric lines must be designed so that no mutual discomfort or hazard results during normal operation, rescue operations, or installation works.
Wherever local conditions are favorable and the characteristics of the electric lines permit it, overhead electric lines crossing the ropeway corridor shall be replaced by underground cables.
The minimum breaking strength of tensioning or regulating ropes shall be at least 5.5 times the maximum axial load in the rope during operation.
Telephonic and signal wire ropes must be of the stranded type and protected against corrosion (such as hot-dip galvanizing or polymer sheathing) to ensure clear communication.
Rope-socketing (splicing or socket-pouring) must be performed with utmost care. Only specialized organizations with proven experience in making rope sockets shall be entrusted with this operation.

A rope must be immediately withdrawn from service when the loss of strength in the rope due to wear, corrosion, broken wires, or a combination thereof is approaching one-sixth (16.67%) of the original strength.
The coefficient of friction (µ) for drive sheave grooves without lining (cast iron or steel) must equal 0.07.
The coefficient of friction (µ) for drive sheave grooves with leather lining must equal 0.15.
The coefficient of friction (µ) for drive sheave grooves with rubber or similar lining must equal 0.25 to prevent slippage.
Drive sheave grooves with aluminum lining may also be used, for which the value of µ must be agreed upon between the ropeway promoter and the Inspecting Authority.
The contact angle of the traction/haulage rope on the driving sheave must ensure that in the most unfavorable combination of circumstances, the required drive power is safely transmitted to the rope.
An automatic mechanical and electrical braking interlock must be triggered instantly if the normal stop or emergency stop push button is pressed by the operator.
